content:
**Observations:**
- Banana plant with leaves drooping and collapsing around the pseudostem
- Significant yellowing visible at the base/lower portions of the leaves
- Leaves are wilting and hanging down rather than standing upright
- Systemic, whole-leaf symptom pattern — no discrete spots or lesions
- Outer/lower leaves appear most affected

**Matching against classes:**
- **Anthracnose**: Dark sunken lesions on fruit — not matching
- **Bunchy Top**: Short, stiff, upright leaves with yellow streaks at margins — not matching (leaves here are large and drooping)
- **Cigar End Rot**: Tip rot on banana fingers — not matching
- **Cordana Leaf Spot**: Oval brown spots with yellow halos — no discrete spots visible
- **Panama Disease**: Fusarium wilt causing yellowing of outer/lower leaves that then collapse and droop around the pseudostem — matches well
- **Yellow and Black Sigatoka**: Yellow streaks turning black/brown on leaf lamina — no streak pattern visible

The collapsed, yellowing leaves drooping around the pseudostem is the hallmark presentation of Panama Disease (Fusarium wilt), which causes systemic vascular wilting.
